import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data from the CSV file
customer_segments = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Convert 'Dt_Customer' column to datetime
customer_segments['Dt_Customer'] = pd.to_datetime(customer_segments['Dt_Customer'])

# Group by 'Dt_Customer' and calculate the total revenue for each month
monthly_revenue = customer_segments.groupby('Dt_Customer').agg({'Z_Revenue': 'sum'})

# Plot the monthly revenue using seaborn's lineplot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.lineplot(x=monthly_revenue.index, y='Z_Revenue', data=monthly_revenue.reset_index())

# Set the title and labels
plt.title('Monthly Revenue Over Time')
plt.xlabel('Date')
plt.ylabel('Total Revenue')

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data from the CSV file
customer_segments = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Convert 'Dt_Customer' column to datetime
customer_segments['Dt_Customer'] = pd.to_datetime(customer_segments['Dt_Customer'])

# Group by 'Dt_Customer' and calculate the total revenue for each month
monthly_revenue = customer_segments.groupby('Dt_Customer').agg({'Z_Revenue': 'sum'})

# Plot the monthly revenue using seaborn's lineplot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.lineplot(x=monthly_revenue.index, y='Z_Revenue', data=monthly_revenue.reset_index())

# Set the title and labels
plt.title('Monthly Revenue Over Time')
plt.xlabel('Date')
plt.ylabel('Total Revenue')

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
